_about: The 1900 Materials' own keying rules, laid over the Jesup workspace's (jesup/config/keying.json) by harness/keying.py. Only what this book prints differently is here; every leaf carries its attestation in _why.
_glyphs: Ruled by the editor off the scan, 2026-11-07: the hooked K and N, the backwards ye, the tall l, the forked d (ð) and ä (Cyrillic а with diaeresis) are folds; ђ һ ѵ с̧ ł and the grave are letters of the notation. The ҕ-like letter is ђ. Ignored, ruled by the editor 2026-11-16: the hook below є (1-252 l7, 1-298 l25 Кэ́l…; the layers read ę) and below һ (1-041 l12), printed inconsistently and with no discernible phonetic or semantic content; the hooked є is keyed є. There is no barred т: what looked like one is the barred l, ł, which the layers read as plain т (the editor, 2026-11-07: 1-102 l4 єłа́, 1-101 l15, 1-075 l11, 1-096 l13, 1-100 l19, 1-076 l6). A plain т is printed in the same word elsewhere (1-077 l12 єто́н), so no fold can tell them apart: a т in a native form is a place to zoom. Unruled forms still reach review: prose_alphabet selects every token that carries anything outside the Russian alphabet.

_why.script_folds.Cyrl.keep: The notation's two Latin letters, which no Cyrillic letter shares a shape with in this face: the tall l (1-024 l20 пы́ӈыlте) and w (1-024 l20 Тот-төмwа́ткен). A word whose other Latin letters are all lookalikes keeps these.
_why.folds.ę: The hook below є is ignored, ruled by the editor 2026-11-16: it is printed inconsistently and carries no discernible phonetic or semantic content (1-024 l34, 1-036 l12, 1-038 l19: the ratified Кэ́lє, 18 times on 7 pages, keyed plain). The layers read the hooked є as Latin e with an ogonek (Кślę, Кэлę).
_why.folds.Ę: The capital of folds.ę, by the same ruling.
_why.numeral_folds.\u0406: Roman numerals are keyed Latin, ruled by the editor 2026-11-16. The layers set Cyrillic І in them, alone and mixed (1-024 l32 IІІ for II; 1-023 l23 І): 5 words І and 5 ІІ in mz/ocr.
_why.numeral_folds.\u0425: As numeral_folds.І: the layers set Cyrillic Х for the numeral (1-024 l38 т. Х; ХІ once in mz/ocr).
_why.script_folds.Cyrl.pairs.a: A Latin letter inside a Cyrillic word is the layer misreading the Cyrillic letter of the same shape, which is how this book is keyed (read-materials-page: a shape both scripts share is Cyrillic). The two copies set 2,015 such words in mz/ocr (ӄol, liэн, аттool, ewђан, Kalє). Ruled by the editor, 2026-11-16, with the condition that nothing Latin is left but keep, so a Latin name with a Russian ending stays whole.
_why.detectors.footnote_paren_opener: Footnote marks are keyed as printed, ruled by the editor 2026-11-16: the reference in the text is a raised digit and a full-size paren (1-024 l2 языка¹)), and the note opens with a full-size digit and paren (1-024 l38 1) Извѣстія…). The Chukchee raises both.
_why.folds.\u049b: The hooked K this book prints is ӄ, as in the modern Chukchi alphabet: ruled by the editor, 2026-11-07. Both Google Books copies read it as қ, a codepoint the print does not use (1-128 l10 қінқäђті; 1-175 Ңэ́ўс̧қäт). Crib: the Jesup q (Qoraˊwg̣ê) and modern ӄ.
_why.folds.\u049a: The capital of folds.қ, by the same ruling (2026-11-07): the OCR's Қ is the printed hooked K, Ӄ.
_why.folds.\u04a3: The hooked N is ӈ, the modern Chukchi letter: ruled by the editor off the scan, 2026-11-07 (1-020 l22, 1-055 l19, 1-082 l3, 1-133 l2, 1-108 l5). The layers read it ң. Crib: Jesup ñ (Ңыро́н = Ñĭroˊn).
_why.folds.\u04a2: The capital of folds.ң, by the same ruling (2026-11-07).
_why.folds.\u04d9: What the layers read as ә is printed as a backwards ye, э: ruled by the editor off the scan, 2026-11-07 (1-034 l2, 1-086 l36, 1-147 l16, 1-178 l14; 1-128 l10).
_why.folds.\u04d8: The capital of folds.ә, by the same ruling (2026-11-07).
_why.folds.\u04cf: The tall l is one letter however the layers read it (l, Ӏ, л, һ): the editor found no visual distinction, 2026-11-07 (1-038 l37, 1-151 l12, 1-027 l8, 1-077 l15, 1-136 l13, 1-323 l25, 1-054 l3, 1-110 l4). The palochka never occurs in Russian prose, so it folds to l whole.
_why.folds.\u04c0: The capital of folds.ӏ: the layers' palochka is the tall l (2026-11-07).
_why.folds.d\u030c: The forked d (a serif D with two spurs from the top centre, like an aquila) is keyed eth, ð: the editor's choice of codepoint, 2026-11-07, its sound unknown. Copy A reads it ď (1-022 l29 -ора́wеďат, 1-142 l16, 1-080 l10, 1-100 l27, 1-174 l25), sometimes ð already (1-169 l14). Crib: Jesup ʟ̣ (oraˊwêʟ̣at). Where a layer reads it ђ no fold can reach it; the scan decides.
_why.folds.D\u030c: The capital of folds.ď, by the same ruling (2026-11-07).
_why.folds.a\u0308: ä is Cyrillic а with a diaeresis, by the rule that a shape both scripts share is keyed Cyrillic: the editor's ruling, 2026-11-07 (1-025 l7, 1-070 l4, 1-080 l2, 1-118 l3). The layers key it Latin; every Latin-only token carrying it is a native form read in Latin letters (lýlkäl, titä), none German.
_why.folds.A\u0308: The capital of folds.ä, by the same ruling (2026-11-07).
_why.inventory.\u0142: The barred l, a horizontal serifed stroke through the centre, keyed ł as the layers have it: the editor's choice, 2026-11-07, as the Polish letter is the nearer sound (1-070 l13, 1-115 l14, 1-175 l5, 1-287 l2). The layers also read it as т (1-102 l4 єта́ for єłа́; _glyphs).
_why.inventory.\u0327: с̧, ruled a letter of the notation by the editor, 2026-11-07 (1-060 l11, 1-129 l2, 1-231 l16, 1-175). The book names it a consonant: note 1 to no. 25 (1-175 l29) says women's pronunciation sets ч, с̧, and р before soft vowels as ц, and рк, чһ as a double ц; the text layer reads that с̧ as plain с. Crib: Jesup s˙ (Neˊᵋs˙qᴀn).
_why.inventory.\u0452: Dje, ruled a letter of the notation by the editor, 2026-11-07 (1-028 l3, 1-070 l3, 1-095 l1, 1-120 l2, 1-170 l1). Crib: Jesup g̣ (-wђе = -wg̣ê).
_why.inventory.\u0402: The capital of inventory.ђ (2026-11-07; Ђа́ďе, informant lines).
_why.inventory.\u04bb: Shha, ruled a letter of the notation by the editor, 2026-11-07 (1-038 l20, 1-132 l2, 1-104 l39, 1-074 l7, 1-128 l3). Shared with Latin h in this face, so keyed Cyrillic. The layers also misread the tall l as һ (1-038 l37, 1-128 l8).
_why.inventory.\u0475: Izhitsa, ruled a letter of the notation by the editor, 2026-11-07 (1-058 l4, 1-092 l13, 1-122 l3, 1-206 l19).
_why.mark_license.\u0306.\u0443: ў is printed throughout the informant lines and the Contents: 1-178 Кутјэ́ўт, 1-161 Ка́ўно, 1-175 Ңэ́ўс̧қäт, 1-019 (Contents, no. 80) Ры́нтеў. Licensed by the editor for this text, 2026-11-06.
_why.mark_license.\u0306.\u0454: A breve over є is printed in 1-054 l21 эјһуlэ́ткє̆lін (read at 2x; copy B a caron). Nothing in the notation rules a breve out of є; licensed by the editor for this text, 2026-11-16.
_why.mark_license.\u0306.\u044b: A breve over ы is printed in 1-182 l19 кы́ры̆ӈы and 1-235 l38 эlу́кы̆н: a rounded cup, the shape of the breve on й in широкій under it, not the pointed circumflex (read at 2x; both copies drop it). Licensed by the editor for this text, 2026-11-16.
_why.mark_license.\u030c.р: A caron over р is printed in native forms, р̌ of the 1899 key (§§ 1–10): 1-036 and 1-038 ја́нр̌а-ка́lат, 1-284 Јанр̌а́-ӈаw, 1-091 l21 аӈа́нр̌ан, 1-104 l4–5 јанр̌а̂́-lа̀ўl and ја́нр̌а-ӈа̀w, 1-126 l9 вінр̌ээс̧ӄі́ўl-і-ѵм, 1-145 l19 ђэӄэнр̌э́т (read at 2x; both copies a plain р). Ratified on each page, then licensed by the editor for this text, 2026-11-17.
_why.mark_license.\u030c.ј: A caron over a dotless ј is printed in 1-114 l24 э́ј̌ӈы: a straight stem with a descender curling left, the ј shape, with a caron where its dot would be, not the V-shaped у of ў (read at 4x; the layers ў). Ruled by the editor at that line, 2026-11-17.
_why.lookalikes.\u04e9: Barred o is a letter of the 1900 notation, printed in the Chukchi forms (1-024 l20 тот-төмwat…, 1-076 l11). The trap is the Jesup one, U+04E9 for U+0275, which this book cannot commit. Unflagged by the editor, 2026-11-06.
_why.tier1_traps.\u04e9: As lookalikes.ө: the same ruling, in the trap table.
_why.lookalike_chars.\u04e9: As lookalikes.ө: the same ruling, in the file gate.
_why.lookalike_greps.\u04e9: As lookalikes.ө: the same ruling, in the Tier-1 worklist.
_why.lookalikes.\u2019: The book prints a curly apostrophe between a native stem and its Russian case ending: 1-022 l19 Ајңаѝва́т’омъ, l37 Ајңаѝва́т’а (read at 2x). It displaces no stress mark, so it is no trap here.
_why.tier1_traps.': Where the text layer has U+0027 the print has the curly ’ (1-022 l19, l37), so that is what a straight apostrophe displaces here, not ˊ.
_why.inventory.\u0301: Stress is printed as an acute over the vowel of a native form: 1-024 l20 …wáткен пы́ңыlте, 1-024 l15 Кутјэ́ўт. Russian prose prints none. The book says so itself: note 7 to no. 3 (1-098 l46) cites ам-ја́ра-wу́рра as printed in the text with the acute moved, ам-јара-wурра́!, 'удареніе въ концѣ для большей выразительности' (stress at the end, for expressiveness). Book-internal apparatus: the acute is stress.
_why.inventory.\u0300: A grave is printed in native forms, confirmed a grave by the editor off the scan, 2026-11-07 (1-037 l24, 1-104 l4, 1-192 l21, 1-260 l41). It is two marks. On a vowel it is secondary stress in a compound, ruled by the editor 2026-11-16: it sits in an element before the last, whose acute is the primary stress (Аӈа̀ӈ-ва́ырђын 1-028, ђырђо̀р-ра́мкын 1-032, чіђэ̀ј-вэ́эм 1-033, еўча̀ӈ / -ра́мкын split at a line end 1-032), and The Chukchee writes both stresses ˊ (añaˊñ-vaˊɪrg̣ɪn, G̣ɪrg̣oˊr-raˊmkin). On a consonant (н д т) it stands where The Chukchee sometimes writes its palatalization dot ˙ (та́н̀ӈыт, taˊn˙ñɪt), but it is printed inconsistently: Эlэ́нд̀і carries it in the introduction (1-026 l21, l28; 1-027 l8) and never in the tale itself (Эlэ́нді six times, 1-395 to 1-405), and The Chukchee has Eleˊndi. Keyed where printed; what the consonant grave marks is open.
_why.detectors.word_medial_caps: The rule catches ɪ ᴇ ʟ ᴀ keyed as capitals; no small capital appears on 1-022, 1-024, 1-026, 1-058, 1-063, 1-070, 1-076 or 1-101 read at 2x, and the text layer holds none in 480 pages.
_why.detectors.dot_above_g: No g̣ on the leaves read for detectors.word_medial_caps; the notation's back consonants are Cyrillic letters, not a marked g.
_why.detectors.suffix_mark_drop: As detectors.dot_above_g: its one table row is g̣ before -ɪ.
_why.detectors.apostrophe_unlicensed: As lookalikes.’: the apostrophe is printed, so a straight one is a slip for ’, not for a stress mark, and it does not make a token Tier-1.
_why.tier2_scripts.Cyrl: This book prints its Chukchi in Cyrillic (1-024 l15 тэ́…ын, Кутјэ́ўт), so a Cyrillic token is judged by its glyphs, never excluded by its script.
_why.prose_alphabet.Cyrl: The pre-1918 Russian alphabet the prose is set in (1-022 throughout: ѣ і ъ), in NFD, so й is и with the breve orthographic_bases already discounts. Left out on purpose: ѵ, a letter of the native forms (1-101 l3 тѵмң-) and all but absent from Russian prose, so a Russian ѵ is a loud question rather than a silent skip; and ё, which NFD splits.
